title: docs(pm-dispatch): cross-repo unlock keys on consumer installability, not upstream merge
body:
Fixes #11498

## What

One boundary clause in the state model's label discipline — the unlock-scan specification — in `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` only:

- **Cross-repo unlock keys on "the consumer can install it", not "upstream merged".** When the consuming repo consumes the upstream as published packages (not a git SHA pin), the unlock scan verifies the fix has reached an installable release before returning the card (install-surface probe: does the installed package accept the new key / new behaviour). Unreleased means the card moves to `pm:on-hold` with a consumer-install-surface `Restart-when:` criterion — never back to `pm:queue`, because a re-queued dispatch is doomed to end premise-false. Release and dependency upgrade are manual acts, so the hold comment pre-writes the wake dispatch shape for any seat to inherit. Pin-consuming repos are excluded, deliberately: a pin move is installability, and the existing pin-lag reading (multi-repo coordination rule 2) already covers them — without this boundary the clause would wrongly hold their cards.

No new mechanism is introduced. Verified against the current file before writing: the `pm:on-hold` state row already accepts a one-line executable `Restart-when:` criterion, `references/state-machine.md` documents the same carrier (read-only here; that file belongs to the sibling card), the daily triage subround already evaluates executable criteria, and half-state patrol H9 admits "a one-line executable predicate". This clause only routes the release-gated case into that existing machinery.

## Placement

The clause lands as a bullet directly after the `Blocked-by:` reverse-index bullet — the sentence that specifies the unlock scan's return-on-close duty, i.e. exactly the clause the incident showed to be under-specified. Multi-repo coordination rule 2 (the dispatch-time pin-lag reading) is cross-referenced, not duplicated. The alternative placement inside rule 2 was considered and rejected: the defect fired at unlock time, and the routing target (`pm:on-hold` plus `Restart-when:`) is state-machine behaviour, which keeps state transitions specified in one section.

## Line-ratchet accounting (ceiling 666, headroom 0)

Net 0 lines (666 before, 666 after), paid by consolidating a rule that was stated twice into its one home — content deletion, not re-wrap:

- The merged-ref file-surface re-verification rule appeared both as unlock-scan duty 3 (the `Blocked-by:` bullet) and restated in full in the selection-priority paragraph. The rationale ("upstream merged does not mean the card still stands — the merge that closed the upstream most likely also fixed your card in passing") moved into the duty-3 parenthetical, and the selection-priority paragraph now points at that duty instead of restating it. No content was dropped; the freed lines are the deleted duplicate.

## Authorization

Maintainer, verbatim (未译, in-session 2026-08-24): 「经验是不是应该写入项目 skills」 → 「写入」.

This PR touches a governed face (`.claude/**`): draft only, human merge (maintainer ruling 2026-08-11, verbatim: 「所有 skills 的更新和 adr 类似,需要人工审核」). No auto-merge, no queue, no ready-flip by any seat.

Sibling card #11499 owns the `references/` lessons and is untouched here; #11499 remains open.
